Further on we shall allude to her family affections and her charity toward the sisters. Suffice it here to say that, through the thousands of letters, carefully preserved by her spiritual daughters, the affectionate heart of Mother Rosa is revealed, made of tenderness and visceral concern. Each of the sisters is for her a gift of God, has a name, an individuality, a personal context. Her expressions of affection, always original and beautiful, not at all conventional, are especially beautiful in the final farewell:

«God bless you: I am your poor Mother» - «The blessing of the eternal Father be with you, mine wholly forever, little daughter. I am your poor Mother Rosa» - «I keep you always present: wherever I go, I always carry with me all my blessed little daughters» - «Greet all the religious for me: tell them that every morning I enclose them in the Heart of Jesus, so too the dear little girls» - «Goodbye, I hold you in the Heart of Jesus, and I am always yours» - «Believe me your Mother, who blesses you and holds you to her bosom, never to leave you again and to call herself always your Mother Rosa».

She educated the sisters in the right measure of affective behavior, as spouses of Jesus, who is a jealous Spouse and must absorb all affection. But when the heart is full of this preferential love, one need not distrust affection for creatures. «God put in your heart the great affection for this your poor Mother — she wrote to Sister A. Celsa Speranza —: it is only God's work, not yours, and there is nothing human at all in it» (12-11-1886).

In her relations with the sisters Mother Rosa was not a slave to formalities. She had grown accustomed to addressing all as «tu»; they felt her thus closer; but the Rule imposed the formal address. Having learned that in some community this norm was not observed, she wrote to the superior:

«Take care: I confess that perhaps this ugly vice must have been introduced because I gave bad example; but from now on it will not happen to me again, and I ask pardon of God and of them for the bad example» (L. to Sr. A. Santina Solenghi: undated, no. 256).

But she did not succeed in keeping the formal address, judging from the letters.

II. SPIRITUAL ITINERARY OF ROSA GATTORNO

[…] 1. Discovering God's design

The family climate, in a special way the example of her mother's piety, fostered in little Rosa a spontaneous attraction to religious manifestations. Having entered adolescence, she began to feel strongly drawn to prayer, seeking solitude. A sister of hers attests: «She was sometimes heard pouring herself out in such ardent aspirations of love of God and, however much she believed herself alone, she did not manage to hide them» (FIOCCHI, I, pp. 11-15; II, p. 256).

Not everything, however, was sweetness of fervor in those years. The amusements in which she took part, as we have seen, however wholesome and justified they might be, became at some moment a source of troublesome disquiet of conscience, anticipation of the future sufferings caused by the distance of her Good. Still in 1873 the enemy continued to torture her with the memory of those anxieties (M 4.1, p. 415).

We have no data on the method of interior life observed by her in the six years of married life, but, judging from that undertaken as soon as she was left a widow, we may suppose that, under the direction of the priest Fr. Giuseppe Firpo, she not only knew how to sanctify the events of family life, but lived all the more assiduously the sacramental life and the practice of prayer, as well as the exercise of charity visiting hospitals and collaborating in other initiatives.

The «conversion»

Rosa Gattorno had the conviction of being a convert, that is, that there had been a moment in her life in which God's mercy drew as it were a dividing line between a past to be erased, because still oriented toward earth, and a new existence to of-

15 For a deeper knowledge of Mother Rosa's affective richness I refer to the very complete study of Maria E. CONVERTINI, Rosa Gattorno: una madre. Generalate House Daughters of St. Anne. Rome 1987. fer to God, having discovered the one Good, for which and in which it is worth living. In her retrospective gaze, when she begins the composition of her Memoirs, she sees thus the change wrought in her in 1858:

«Remaining free of every bond, I devoted myself with more fervor to pious works and to visiting the hospitals and the poor sick at home, helping them as much as I could and serving them in everything.

By the grace of the Lord I perceived that all earthly affections were dissipating; nothing was any longer tasty to me; only my God was the pasture of all my delights.

The sorrows of family were without equal. I poured everything into the heart of my dear Crucified: for Him alone — I kept repeating to myself — all my suffering is little! Because I had committed many sins, I could not wholly give up certain little things, because, living together in the family, it was not granted me. Oh! how much I had to fight!!!» (M 1.1).

We already know what those many sins could have been; so they appeared in her eyes when her spirit was now flooded by the splendor of the holiness of God. She felt in her inmost being as it were a debt of love to be paid at any cost. Thus was born her insatiable thirst for penances; she herself says so next, in a heroic outpouring of love:

«Always clasped to my Good, I went on repeating: Oh! my sins deserve worse and hell itself; and most willingly I go to feel those pains, provided I be led by you and near and clasped: you alone are my paradise! And I wept much for having offended Him. With the permission of obedience I increased as much as I could the penances…» (M 1.1, p. 25).

But the Lord came to relieve her of that weight. Repeatedly, while she was in contemplation, He made her see two books, held by two angels. In the first, «quite beautiful and not so thick», was written: a list of names, with the addition: And then saints; at the end of the list was her name very visible, with the inscription: And then saint. In the other book, «which was thick», she saw written her own sins, «but all canceled I saw them — she relates — with the blood of my dear Redeemer». At the end, here too was her name, with the same addition: And then saint.

p. 954

The fear, however, of not having been totally forgiven comes back to torment her. One day she saw those sins covered by a black veil, and wept inconsolably, until the veil was lifted. Later, in confirmation of the pardon sealed by God, she saw over the canceled sins now a palm, now a most beautiful crown; this was then replaced by the crown of thorns to her great joy. She exclaims at the end of the account:

«Oh! poor sinner! Oh! goodness of a God the Father! Who would not destroy himself for this dear Father? It is truly nothing to give Him all ourselves in comparison with so great an immensity of greatness. Oh! goodness without limits! (M 1.1, pp. 5-7).

The more she discovered the greatness of divine mercy the more she saw herself, in the presence of the supreme Good and loving Father, as «a miserable sinner, a loathsome worm of the earth»; but she reacted full of gratitude and security: «It is no longer I who live, it is my Jesus who lives in me!» (cf. Gal 2:20).

Still in 1862 she felt pursued by the tempter with the fear of not having merited God's pardon, because her sins had not been well confessed. She would have wished to redo the general confession; fortunately her director, Fr. Firpo, did not permit her to return to the past life. Finally, peace regained, she felt the Lord's reproach: «Was it not enough for you to have seen everything canceled?» (M 1.1, pp. 27-29).

The assurance of pardon will not prevent her, however, from finding in the memory of the offenses done to God a motive for humbling herself with expressions like this: «My wickednesses permit nothing, because I am infamous» (M 1.1, p. 39, year 1866). […]

She decides on total consecration to God

The past now erased and the future entrusted to God's design, Rosa remained waiting for what He might wish to manifest to her. The moment had come to seal with fundamental commitments the choice made. In 1858, as soon as her husband died, she had bound herself with the vow of chastity for a year; on the feast of the Immaculate Conception of that same year, with the approval of her director, she made perpetual vows of chastity and obedience; four years later she had authorization to add the vow of poverty. It was like the beginning of a new life, she will comment later in her Memoirs:

«I laid everything at the feet of Mary, that she might make a gift of it to my Good Jesus and beg Him to accept me as spouse. Oh! what I felt! as if I had entered another state of living, and I did not know whether I lived or who lived for me» (M 1.1, p. 2).

It is not specified whether the vow of obedience was in relation to the spiritual Father nor what was its scope. The fact is that Rosa did not remain satisfied; it seemed to her she had reserved what above all required a donation of love: the will. And one day she wished to sacrifice it with a vow:

«One thing remained to me that I had not made to Him in sacrifice and vow, and it was, oh my Beloved! my will. And in fact I made renunciation of it to Him, telling Him that this vow was certainly not worthy to remain together with the other vows, because with it I had so many times offended Him, so that I placed it under His feet, and begged Him to deign to use it as a footstool. Only to live I wish of your love, oh sweet Love of mine! (M 1.1, p. 20).

These experiences are situated in the months of her stay at S. Francesco d'Albaro, a country locality to which she had moved to recover her health. It was for her almost a providential retreat at that decisive moment of the orientation of her life. In that peace she experienced with greater intensity intimacy with God and the lights of contemplation, while discovering unequivocally her special vocation to a life of sufferings. It was the answer received from her director Fr. Firpo after having ascertained that every consolation of spirit that was given her was always preceded and followed by lacerating days of aridity, of abandonment, of fears and temptations, of ugly diabolical suggestions. From now on love and suffering will be inseparable in her life, indeed suffering will be her way of loving. And, in her logic of loving expiation, she will opt to double the corporal penances.

On 24 September 1861 she made, in the church of S. Francesco d'Albaro, the profession of the Rule of the Franciscan Third Order; three

In fact, she could not fail to find in the stigmatized one of La Verna, living copy of the Crucified, her model of crucified life.

4. Mother Rosa, teacher of prayer

From the first day of the foundation she organized the novitiate of Piacenza with an intense schedule of life of prayer and, therefore, in an environment of retreat. She herself directed the morning meditation, generally on the Passion of Christ, with accents full of unction, with the aim of setting the young religious on the way to the practice of mental prayer. In her instructions to the novices she gave primary importance to contemplative prayer. But the most effective lesson was she herself, her example, her hours of contemplation, her habitual absorption in God, as also her words full of fervor and of higher light, that gentle and penetrating gaze of hers which silently questioned, and the whole bearing of one who breathes the atmosphere of the divine. She was for all the best stimulus to commit themselves seriously on the ways of the search for God.

From the brief recommendations that we find in her letters to the sisters we can deduce what the exhortations were that she made by word of mouth, in personal conversations and in conferences, especially on the occasion of visits:

«Prayer is our only shield of defense» - «It is the key of graces» - «Do not forget to be always in the presence of God the Father; remember the instructions that this miserable one gave you» - «Ah! what joy to be united to the good God! But you, my dear, if you stay far from this most loving Spouse, what will you ever have? nothing. Go, go suck the honey of sweetness; He is its essence, so run to his fountain and drink, get drunk!…» (to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 5-12-1868, 18-9-1869, 16-1-1870, 14-11-1873; to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino: 3-12-1872).

In a special way she recommended attention and fidelity to the inspirations of God, which requires the spirit of prayer that disposes to listening to the divine calls. «Woe to that creature who has made herself deaf to the inspirations that God, in his mercy, gives her» (Lett. to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 21-12-1868).

5. Alone and without a guide on the hard road

One of the most persistent interior sufferings in the life of Rosa Gattorno is the problem of spiritual direction.

As a young woman she had as confessor the priest Fr. Antonio Accinelli, vice-pastor of the cathedral, with whom she took counsel at the time of contracting marriage. Later she put herself under the direction of Fr. Giuseppe Firpo, custodian of the metropolitan church; he was of great help to her in the first months of widowhood, at the moment of her decision to consecrate herself to the Lord and during her stay at S. Francesco d'Albaro. Rosa opened her interior to him with full trust, submitted to his obedience her every initiative, especially regarding bodily penances; and he took seriously the task of guiding her, having realized that it was a generous soul, extraordinarily favored by God, as appears from the letters, of profound ascetical content, written to his spiritual daughter in those years.

But suddenly Rosa interrupted, on her own initiative, the direction, limiting herself to confession alone; until in May 1865 she left him completely, to the great regret of the good priest, who accepted such a decision with humility, fearing he himself had given the reason. Rosa, in her Memoirs, seems to hint at certain divergences or difficulties that made her suffer and prepared the change of director. In 1861 she complained to the Lord: «I have no one of whom to ask opinion and counsel: you have taken everything from me, I have only you, my Spouse!» (M 1.1, p. 10). There was a moment when Fr. Firpo, seeing her suffer because of diabolical vexations and not knowing what to do, wished to have recourse to exorcisms, obtaining the license from the archbishop, which Rosa curtly refused to accept (M 1.1, pp. 31, 555). «Several times I would have wished to turn to some learned priest — she adds —, but Jesus did not want it; and so I stayed with the one he had assigned me» (M 1.1, p. 57).

In 1864 she had begun to confess to Fr. Luigi Cogrossi, with the consent of the archbishop; this priest had a reputation for holiness and Rosa had gone to visit him in his native town, Castelleone, diocese of Cremona. Fr. Cogrossi then accompanied her to Rome, when she was received in audience by Pius IX, and introduced her to various persons of prominence in ecclesiastical circles.

The Servant of God relates how, on returning from Rome, determined to begin the foundation of the Institute in Piacenza, her confessor — probably Fr. Firpo — disapproved of what she had done (M 2, p. 45). The affair had a happy ending at the beginning of 1867 when Rosa, now foundress, re-established filial relations with her former director (cf. FIOCCHI, I, pp. 22f, 31, 38, 52-56, 66, 174f, 300f).

Mother Rosa continued under the guidance of the Cremonese priest in Piacenza as well; she had him as chaplain of the first community, indeed as the first ecclesiastical superior, until she dismissed him in the month of August 1867.

Before that date, however, the foundress had discovered in Fr. Giovanni Battista Tornatore, priest of the Mission, known in Piacenza for his doctrine and ascetical life, the man sent to her by Providence to counsel her in those first steps of the Institute and also in the perplexities of her spirit. The role he had in the orientation of the foundation has earned him, on the part of the Daughters of St. Anne, recognition of the title of co-founder.

From the first moment the difficulty appeared of reconciling the external relationship, concerning the work, with the internal one of spiritual direction. The foundress became aware of a certain incompatibility with the pious and austere religious on account of the different spiritual experience. She herself mentions it:

«Not knowing where to go to confess, the desire came to me to go to Signor Tornatore, and the first times I liked it; but then it caused me a something of fear: his direction was so different from my old one! Enough, I cared little, because my guide was my Jesus in everything and for everything» (M 2, p. 555).

In reality, the whole year 1869 she felt «alone, without comfort» (M 1.2, p. 29). A hard blow to her sensibility of faith was the unjust harshness used toward her on 31 March 1869 by Fr. Tornatore, a victim of the

A reading of the archive documents, in Virga Jesse, n.s. 4 (1988) no. 6, pp. 16-21; 5 (1989) no. 1, pp. 18-25. deceptions of the superior of the community, who deprived her even of communion (cf. M 1.2, pp. 21-29). She, however, continued under his direction.

This heroic faith in God's representative was put to the test again in January 1870, when she learned, by divine light, that her director was going about saying things of her spirit. She was determined to leave him, but the soul of Fr. Bernardo appeared to her, who commanded her to return to the guidance of the co-founder (M 1.1, pp. 89, 92).

At the end of 1870 Mother Rosa complained: «Oh! blessed those souls who have their direction that comforts them, assures them, lifts them up! But I?…» (M 1.1, p. 94). Similar laments, often very bitter, will be repeated from time to time in the following years, especially in the moments of aridity and of withdrawal of her Good, when she feels alone, abandoned in the most cruel darkness. One of the reasons for which she feels the lack of a director is not knowing whether her penances, so exquisite, are according to God's will, or mere satisfaction of her craving for suffering. Usually everything ends with the certainty that Jesus communicates to her directly: I am your guide. At other times the voice of her Good reaches her through mysterious intermediaries: one is the aforementioned Fr. Bernardo, the other a luminous cloud that comes to her aid by clearing up her uncertainties or manifesting hidden things to her. So she expresses herself at the beginning of 1871:

«Behold I need to know certain hidden things: and my Love himself comes, instructs me as master, provides me with most sublime knowledge, sustains me in certain struggles. Alone I find myself, but no one do I desire, because my Good helps me, directs me, comforts me, gives me life… My cloud is always near me and is quite red; and because it suggests to me and teaches me, I hear a voice that comes out of it. Oh! sweetness without equal!…» (M 1.1, p. 107).

In the same year 1871 Fr. Tornatore, concerned about Mother Rosa's health, wished to forbid her privations in food; hence a new reason to close herself ever more to his direction (M 1.2, p. 42f). But the decisive cut of communication, not only in the

M 1.1., p. 89f, 94f, 130, 157, 175, 177; 3, p. 12, 14, 63f; 4.1, p. 18f, 1045; Labors and Consolations, p. 6. internal forum, but also in what concerned the direction of the Institute, was given by the order that came from Rome in February 1872 to the co-founder himself with the drastic prohibition to approach in the future the Daughters of St. Anne and to receive their confessions, all because of the part he had had in the drafting of the text of the Rules. On the following 13 March, in asking for the Father's prompt return, she had the desire to take up his direction again (M 3, pp. 3, 7). In that situation she had recourse to the Holy Spirit, and in him found light and strength, as appears in some of the notes of the same year:

«I feel it is affirmed to me by my governing Spirit. What a consolation it is for me, who am so abandoned by all human help, to have my dear Spirit, who guides me in everything and sustains me so well!…» - «Since my director is God, the Being who lives for me, He made me feel how He wished me to offer Him three penances…» - «A voice said to me: I am your Master, be calm! The peace of conscience I enjoy is such that I see there is a most powerful Spirit who rules and governs me». - «How many beautiful things He told me and taught me, in particular for the Work!… How many caresses when He says to me: My Rosa, courage, for I am with you! do not doubt!» - «Alone as I find myself…, but it is no confusion to me, because all the points are resolved for me one by one by my Jesus. I feel and more clearly I see myself guided by my Spirit. My cloud for some time stays far away…» (M 3, p. 11f, 26; 4.1, p. 4, 6).

But the terrible trial of the abandonment of God supervened, and then she filled her diary with heartrending cries:

«Ah! how painful is my present state! My poor soul, alone, an anchorite in the midst of the great world, an orphan…, is when it finds itself desolate and immersed in the most bitter tribulations…, has lost its Being, finds it nowhere…» - «Alone! Not even from anyone a word of comfort. Alone! alone! in the midst of so great a Work… And then so many souls as I know how to direct, the responsibility for these…: alone! with no one to tell what my soul suffers!…» (M 3, p. 27f, 555).

To the solitude caused by aridity was added the fear of erring, indeed of taking the suggestions of the enemy for the voice of God, of being the cause of some disaster to the Work of God (M 4.1, p. 445, 44-79, 665; March-April 1873).

In the month of June 1873 she felt a strong and repeated impulse to confide herself fully to some priest, whose name she did not wish to say, informing him of everything, even of what passed secretly between God and her, because by now that situation had become unbearable to her; she feared that this too was suggested by the enemy or fashioned by her own mind. She turned to her Good begging Him to give her light on what to do; the resistance was strong:

«My Beloved, you alone, you alone! Ah! continue to be my guide; do not permit me to have to tell anyone whatsoever what you deign to communicate to me! It is now 20 years that the world has not been aware of my things: now, that I am so wasted, must I ever undergo so much grief? At the mere thought I feel faint. You, my Good, know how much it cost me to have to give certain writings and tell my things to a single person: how shall I manage with others besides?… Let me stay as I am. Tell me yourself how I am to conduct myself in everything and do not permit that I have to turn to others» (M 4.1, pp. 71-75).

The inner voice insisted: «Have recourse to the one I told you to go to!» (M 4.1, p. 76f). In fact, in the month of June she seems to have attempted to begin a relationship with the same person for the purpose of direction (M 4.1, pp. 96-99). It was perhaps Fr. Agostino Donadio, of the order of Minims († 1907), with whom Mother Rosa maintained from 1870 a spiritual correspondence of a certain intimacy; this relationship, maintained until death, does not seem to have reached the degree of true direction. The fact is that she continued to feel alone. In the same month of June she wrote: «I have no one to whom to say a word. There are moments when I feel I am dying; what I feel God alone sees; alone I stifle everything…» (M 4.1, p. 103). Then there were added further scruples, indeed the fear of «going mad» (M 1.2, pp. 55, 58, 68). A voice, which often seemed an insidious temptation, whispered to her continually: «Do you think you do well to guide yourself? And are you sure that everything is of God?». But the Lord did not fail her in difficult moments (M 4.2, p. 65), and reassured her: «I am your guide, your comfort» (M 4.2, pp. 44, 76).

At the beginning of 1875, and again in 1877, she took counsel with some priest, perhaps with the confessor of the community of Piacenza, whom she esteemed highly, but only regarding her penances (M 4.3, p. 14; 4.4, pp. 96-98, 1015). In all these years she continues to lament:

p. 962

«Alone in this land of exile!» - «Alone, without human comfort!» - «Alone, alone! There is not a creature to whom I can say a word» - «My God, how painful is my state, full of anguish over certain extraordinary things that the Lord works in me, having no one to turn to!» - «Alone, without anyone to say a word to! Jesus, you know well that you have placed me so and kept me so: you do not want me to turn to anyone… It is your doing, my God!» - «Alone with my beloved Master I am» (M 1.2, pp. 27, 90, 101, 109f; 4.4, pp. 110, 1165, 121).

In the month of June 1880, during the visit to the houses, she had the good fortune to make her confession with «a holy religious», much favored by God. She lost consciousness before receiving absolution, without the confessor noticing. Then she wrote in her notes:

«How much it is worth to have a good and learned director at certain moments! Yes, my God, to be guided by a learned and holy man, as I had the luck to find for confession: O my Jesus! you truly did me the grace of finding a saint; oh! how well he read in my soul!» (M 4.5, pp. 83-185, 212).

In March 1884, finally, she was convinced that she had found the «learned and holy» director in Fr. Bernardino of Portogruaro, who since 1869 had been minister general of the Friars Minor, a truly extraordinary man, under whose government his Order undertook the restoration after a century of suppressions and ruins. But God permitted that the confessions made with him should be a new cause of disturbance. Shortly after she wrote:

«I am alone, Jesus has abandoned me!… I go to confess, and what does he say to me? When I say to him: I am full of sins, I cannot distinguish them, — Calm yourself, where are they?… So will it be because my Good will not like me to put myself in the hands of another's obedience apart from Him?» (M 5.2, pp. 355, 47-49).

Hearing read the lives of the saints, who had the help of a guide, she felt envy. On 29 August of the same year Jesus assured her that it was his will that she put herself under the direction of the Father General; and she promised to tell him everything without reserve, even if it should

23 We do not know whether she should be identified with that «son of St. Francis of Assisi» who came to meet her, when she found herself alone, without a road, as she relates in the book Labors and Consolations (p. 27f). Besides, the whole book may be called an anxious walking alone, without a guide, not knowing whether she has lost the way. cost her a thousand agonies. But on the 31st of the same month she discovered in her inmost being the true cause of that resistance: having to renounce the comfort of the direct guidance of Jesus:

«While I see that the will of my Good is clear that I give to the one I said above my direction, yet I think that my Love, if He wants this, then He will leave me, will no longer come to tell me what I must do; in short, He will no longer act as my master, but will let me have everything to receive from the one who guides me. Oh! piercing thought!… Oh! what will become of me? how shall I be able to get used to it?» (M 5.2, pp. 73, 808, 84, 91-93).

The resistance continued, despite her disposition to put herself under the Father's obedience; every page of the diary faithfully reflects the strong tension of the spirit:

«Oh! when I lived under the sole direction of my Good…! but now, oh! how hard is this state! Certainly, I deserved it, because too many times I complained of being alone. But now, how do I find myself?… Alone and worse than alone!… O my Love, where are you? Why have you so barbarously left me? If you do not want me to be under direction, oh! a single sign, and once more alone!… Oh! how I suffer for having given, in some way, the direction of my soul… » - «But tell me, my Love, was it not you who worked in me when with such force you commanded me to give that religious my direction?…» - «O my Love, why now do you want me directed by a minister of yours? It pains me, because I was too badly accustomed: no direction satisfies me, however learned it be… I cannot adapt…» (M 5.3, pp. 6f, 17, 24-28, 325).

They were months of terrible suffering, those of 1884 and the beginning of 1885. She feared she had gone too far, especially in giving her intimate writings to the confessor to read. She repeats full of bitterness: «What have I done?». In a moment of supreme grief she exclaims: «O Jesus, my Good! if I manage to get out of this, surely I would never again do the same! I suffer too much!» (M 5.3, pp. 32-36, 51).

In March 1885 she says she suspended the direction, «out of a strong repugnance», perhaps on the occasion of her third journey to Sicily. It was indeed on this journey that, passing through Naples, she met again Fr. Gennaro Granito Pignatelli of Belmonte, a priest since 1879, and established with him a deep spiritual friendship. Shortly after she began their correspondence, which became ever more frequent. She had to explain to him her sufferings regarding direction. Perhaps the formula she expresses on returning to Rome was suggested by him: «Subject, but not bound nor tied» to Fr. Portogruaro (M 5.3, p. 57), that is, attentive to the light received from the Lord. The situation nevertheless continued difficult throughout the year 1885 (M 4,3, pp. 60, 63, 68, 70-72, 82, 90-92, 99; 5.4, pp. 19f, 265, 39, 59f). She offered to the Lord that arid obedience, to which she had bound herself by vow (M 5.4, p. 69). Indeed, she blessed God, because thus she felt free from attachment to the spiritual Father, which often, in the sisters, takes away freedom from the spirit, as she was able to observe in the visits to the communities (M 5.4, pp. 100f; 5.5, pp. 15-19, 53, 71f).

In Fr. Bernardino's long absences it was still worse, because the ordinary confessor limited himself to hearing the accusation and giving her absolution. There were not lacking days of light and peace in loving union with the supreme Good; often too comfort came to her from the soul of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, first superior of the house of Palermo, who died on 7 June 1885, a true example of holiness.

In 1887 relations with Fr. Gennaro Granito di Belmonte became more frequent and had by now become true spiritual direction, to the point of giving him a good part of the writings to read, without however the knowledge of Father Bernardino, which gave rise to new worries for her (M 5.5, pp. 86-89; Lett. to Fr. Gennaro: 24-9-1887). From this good Father for two years now she had received only curt answers, and she never asked him anything about her interior; from his reasonings she had the impression that he did not understand her. She had the idea of changing director, entrusting herself to one with whom she communicated without effort; but the Lord made her understand that it was not suitable for her, «because the Work would suffer harm from it». And, as other times, she heard it said: «Be calm: I am your director and master… They will never come to understand you, since I am the artificer of the work that takes place in you» (M 9.2, pp. 3-5, 10-12). She wrote again in February 1888, not without a critical recollection of the bonds of the past:

«A confusion: shall I always have done wrong?… What it means not to have a guide who makes and puts a little order! I would never advise a human creature to remain without a guide, never! And the guide must be learned, so as never to permit promises and vows for an indefinite time; no! everything for a time, because illnesses come, age, sorrows or infirmity…: and what comes of it? What happens to me!» - «I am an exile in the midst of the great world…, I have no one to say a word to…» - «Alone! everything is darkness and pain to me… I believed I was understood by my guide, but no! quite the contrary! Oh! wretched the soul that never has the fortune of being understood! I see my state clearly, but when I set it out, I see that they take one thing for another… Oh! only those souls will be able to understand me who have loved much and then find themselves down in the most miserable abyss» (M 9.2, p. 23; 9.3, pp. 2, 6, 21; 9.4, p. 7, 38).

She decided, therefore, to put herself fully under the guidance of Fr. Gennaro, although continuing to make her confession with Father Bernardino; so it seems one may deduce from an undated letter to Fr. Gennaro himself. But she had to convince herself once again that it did not enter God's plans that she should have any comfort in spiritual direction: on the one hand the distance and having to make herself known by letter, on the other the realization that even her dear Fr. Gennaro, so clear-sighted in other affairs and in the problems of the Institute, seemed instead, by God's permission, to understand nothing of what concerned the interior of his spiritual daughter. In the following years the same laments return in the Memoirs because she feels alone, the same envy of the souls who have the good fortune to have a director, the same inner voice that assures her: «I am your guide» (M 9.5, pp. 92-113; 9.6, pp. 1-8; 11.2, pp. 71f, 75-77, 89; 12.1, pp. 36, 45f, 1525).

Father Bernardino of Portogruaro ended his term as general in 1889; he died in 1895. Mons. Granito di Belmonte was assigned to Paris, in 1893, as attaché of that nunciature and, in 1899, named apostolic nuncio in Brussels; Mother Rosa, who always maintained with him a spiritual correspondence of great trust, had the joy of attending his episcopal consecration, in the church of the Generalate House, on 26 November of the same year.

The last confessor of the Servant of God was the Capuchin Fr. Vincenzo d'Alatri, who assisted her at the moment of flying to the blessed homeland. Will there have been verified, in that supreme hour, what she foresaw and left written almost three decades earlier?

«He made me see what will happen at my death…; and whoever will have ascendancy over Him (Jesus in the sacrament) will be the one who will have my last direction, that I shall live by obedience, but he will take care not to command me things that he has not first felt well within himself» (M 1.1, p. 164).

III. CHARISMATIC GIFTS AND MYSTICAL PHENOMENA

We arrive at the theme that most attracts attention in the life of the great mystics and that, at the same time, raises greater difficulties from the scientific point of view; indeed, in our case, it is precisely what has put the question mark over the psychic normality of Rosa Gattorno.

In general, the prejudice against bodily mystical phenomena comes from their spectacular character, that is, from the suspicion that, at bottom, there is nothing but the unconscious wish for exhibitionism. Hence unbelieving or simply positivist scientists register all these phenomena — visions, raptures, stigmatizations, diabolical vexations — under certain common denominators of the field of psychiatry: hysteria, hallucinations, erotic sublimations… It must be said, however, that, in the case of Rosa Gattorno, any motive of exhibitionism is precisely to be excluded. Her great concern, throughout her life, was to ensure that no one noticed what there might be of the extraordinary in the gifts of God, as well as in her bodily mortifications. If she had not written her Memoirs and the confidential letters to Fr. Gennaro Granito di Belmonte, everything would have remained hidden. She wrote on 21 May 1876:

«I overcame myself to manifest a certain thing that, out of shame, I had resolved not to say. Oh! how much it costs me to say what my good does in me! Oh! a thousand times I would say in public the horrendous sins I committed, but the graces He grants me, ah! for me is the most painful pain I can have» (M 4.4, p. 625).

Let us try to bring to light this aspect of her spiritual physiognomy, keeping in mind however that it is not the extraordinary gifts, even the most authentic, that demonstrate a person's holiness, all the more since, as was said at the beginning, the problem always remains of distinguishing the field of God's action from the field of the subject's own elaboration.

First of all it is necessary to recall the doctrine of the great master of Mysticism St. John of the Cross on the criteria of discernment to be applied to every extraordinary phenomenon. He warns, concretely, about «locutions», since there are spiritual persons who, «with great facility, form words and reasons, so that it seems to the subject that it is not he who does all this, but that another person interiorly suggests to him the reasons, the answers and the teachings. And indeed he himself reasons with himself and answers himself as if he were one person with another; and in some way it may be said that it is so, for, although the human spirit is the one that operates, nevertheless it is helped by the Holy Spirit to produce and form those true concepts, words and reasons…» *.

The holy doctor does not affirm that these are hallucinations, but a true divine action which the subject perceives in his own way, according to the facility of giving form to what he experiences. The mystic, in fact, finding himself in that zone, still very peripheral, of the unitive process, between infused recollection and rapture — that is, in full possession of the sensory and intellectual faculties — translates his own unusual experience into visual, auditory, tactile, imaginative forms, without realizing that everything is a product of his own creativity, albeit under the supernatural operation. Which takes nothing from the sincerity of the mystic. Such creativity will be more or less fecund according to temperament, sensibility, fantasy and personal situations.

Now, among the human qualities offered by the rich feminine personality of Rosa Gattorno one is her creative and figurative fecundity, that is, the art of transposing common realities into a symbolic and allegorical key. Her book Labors and Consolations is the most splendid demonstration of it.

I think, therefore, that the question of the supernatural character or not of the various phenomena of the survey that follows is out of place: it suffices to rely on the absolutely irreproachable sincerity with which the Servant of God commits to paper the moment she lived, just as she perceived it.

Another premise to keep in mind: Mother Rosa enumerates without end interior lights, penetrations of hearts, foresight of future events, visions…, but never speaks of revelations, never of messages to bring to anyone, and we never see her regulate her own way of behaving and her own decisions according to what she has seen or understood, although sometimes she feels in duty bound to warn, in the

24 Ascent of Mount Carmel, II, 29,1f. strictest secrecy, her confidants. She feels guided by God, taught and sustained by her Good, which gives her such confidence and security, in what concerns the Lord's Work, that she faces with serenity every disagreeable situation, precisely because she is convinced of being a pure and useless instrument of the divine design. But on this consciousness of her mission as foundress we shall dwell further on.

1. Interior charismatic gifts

Besides the ineffable lights and communications, which are part of the infused contemplative experience, as we saw in the preceding chapter, there are also certain gratuitous gifts, perceived within under various forms or symbols, on which Mother Rosa herself provides us with quite precise data.

Light of discernment - Penetration of the interior of persons

At the beginning of the foundation, one day Rosa heard from Jesus these words, in answer to her desire to be useful to the souls entrusted to her:

«Every time you happen to see and penetrate certain hearts, you will see them thus. What you ask of me for the good of the souls who are with you and of whom you have the care, I will give you all, so also for what you desire for priests: precisely what with prayer you will wish me to give them I will give. You will distinguish clearly the good from the bad, I will make you feel an abhorrence when they have indecent ideas against chastity: at once you will feel it and have warning, do not doubt… So for false devout women you will have special lights to distinguish well…» (M 1.1, p. 63).

Gift of God or special natural intuition, or both together, the fact is that she constantly experienced an extraordinary faculty of penetrating the interior of the intentions and situations of persons, in a particular way of her spiritual daughters; as the sisters themselves and the other persons who frequented her also noted with wonder: they were convinced that Mother Rosa read consciences. […]

The inner voice - The cloud - The friendly souls

In moments of perplexity or of darkness and abandonment, in which she feels alone, without the guidance of a director — as has been said — she suddenly feels in her interior a voice that communicates to her security, peace, light on the problem to be faced. Sometimes it is the answer to her prayer: «Tell me, my Beloved, what must I do?». Often it is a reproach for some infidelity or some resistance to what God wants. The voice of the supreme Good becomes at other times a sensible form of divine help in the form of true dictation of what she must write or say to persons. She writes in the month of November 1873:

«I have letters to write. Since I am an ignorant beast, He dictates to me what I must say. I am in the presence of persons, it being a matter of interesting things of the Work: a thing happens in me, that it seems within me a person speaks for me, because the words come out of me without my knowing what I say. I feel and understand that they are not mine, because I would not be capable of saying them: my God, He makes speak, makes work the most ignorant of creatures, as I am» (M 4.2, p. 155) […].

In the Memoirs she also very often speaks of certain intermediary voices, like the one that seemed to come from the bosom of a cloud to guide her in the absence of another guide. Of this cloud she already speaks in 1869:

«Every time I have need, it advises me, answers me what I must do, how I must conduct myself, and I feel comforted in my adversities» - «I always see it at my sides…, and a voice comes out that fills me with paradise and I remain absorbed… I look at it and ask it: Suggest, for I do not know what to say, my Being, my dear Love! Because I am convinced that it is He who is within, and I hear the voice…» (M 1.1, pp. 85-87).

The nearness of the supreme Good, who assists and guides her, is perceived by Mother Rosa in the company of some friendly souls, that is, of deceased persons with whom she has felt and feels herself spiritually bound. One of these souls is that of the holy lay Capuchin Brother Francesco of Camporosso, who died in 1866, canonized in 1962; another, that of Fr. Bernardo Clausi, whom we already know; very often she speaks of the help received from him in the doubts and uncertainties that afflict her; there are the souls of some daughters of St.

Signs and foresight of future events

It is proper to persons of faith, who live in the certainty of God's loving providence over human affairs, to be on the watch for the signs through which such love manifests itself. Rosa Gattorno is convinced of being the object of a particular assistance of her Good, also in what concerns the immediate future. And very often she can verify that the predictions correspond to the truth. Not always, however, does she succeed in interpreting the meaning of the signs, and then she remains waiting for what will happen.

Such signs take various forms. Sometimes she sees a veil of sadness on the face of the Lord or his Heart painfully pierced; at other times the veil of sadness covers the face of Mother St. Anne. One of the most frequent signs is that of one or more stars, which she interprets as an announcement of the death of some daughter of St. Anne; if the star is large, the deceased is a superior. A foreboding too of the near death of some person is the sight of a skull or a skeleton; the first of these warnings she had in the form of a vision in 1857 when she saw the image of Jesus of Nazareth with the features of a skeleton, a presage of her husband's death (FIOCCHI, I, p. 35). There is also another sign: an «ugly beast» that announces ill-omened things to her; she calls it «the courier of bad weather» (M 3, p. 68). She foresees wars, epidemics, famines and other public calamities, as well as the success or failure of certain affairs. Very often she has knowledge of things that happen at a distance; she writes, for example in a letter to Fr. Gennaro Granito di Belmonte: «It happens in a house, in America: painful things! I see everything… But must I say everything?» (Lett. undated no. 345).

Some of the knowledge at a distance and of the predictions seem to correspond to the truth, because they are confirmed by the testimonies of the Process; in five of the letters to the Princess of Fitalia, she noted her surprise on finding that everything had come true as Mother Rosa had written to her (cf. L 8-3-1891, 14-3-1891, 16-3-1897, 29-6-1897). On the other hand, of certain predictions of political events there is reason to doubt that they were true prophecies, since they are probably recollections written after the events had occurred and, therefore, a retrospective reading of them. […]

2. Visions and representations

It is not easy to distinguish visions from signs and apparitions under various figures, just as it is not possible to classify them according to the classical scheme: intellectual, imaginary, corporeal. Indeed, since almost always Rosa Gattorno experiences them in the night hours, more precisely in the half-sleep, it cannot even be determined, very often, whether they are dreams or true representations. Sometimes she speaks of true dreams, like the one she tells the Princess of Fitalia in a letter: she saw her mother dressed as a daughter of St. Anne in paradise (L 8-1-1896) or the other about a fact that had really occurred to the same addressee, as the latter noted in the margin (L 23-1-1896).

From «when she was a little girl» — she will recall it in 1870 — she was already favored by God with «beautiful visions» (M 1.1, p. 88). In 1859, in Genoa, during the novena of Our Lady of the Vineyards, so rich in profound experiences and consolations, she had important visions (M 1.1, p. 3). In the following years they were ever more frequent and very varied: of the person of Christ, of Our Lady, of St. Anne, of St. Michael, of St. Francis of Assisi, of groups of angels, of the glory of heaven, of purgatory, of hell. There are not lacking symbolic and enigmatic visions, whose meaning she herself cannot explain, like

What this sight produced in me I cannot express: a union, a fire that devoured me! But, stupid, I took no account of it, believing it was a common thing. Oh! how great is the goodness of my Jesus!» (M 1.1, p. 2) 28.

Rosa Gattorno, far from being an exhibitionist visionary, always kept secret this gift too of divine goodness; only to paper did she entrust the manifold representations. 3. Bodily mystical phenomena Raptures and ecstasies

That stage of infused prayer that receives the name of ecstatic seems to have begun simultaneously with the first visions in 1859. The first description of an ecstasy properly so called is found, in Rosa Gattorno's recollections, among the graces received in 1861. Before the Blessed Sacrament exposed she had a vision of the blood of the Redeemer; then she adds:

«I remained in ecstasy and did not know, could no longer say anything; and everything is little and a nothing that can be said to a God so merciful toward a poor ignorant creature. After a good while I turned to my Father St. Francis, to all the seraphim and cherubim: that they might sing hymns of grace and thanksgiving for me to my God» (M 1.1, p. 12).

It seems that it was a gentle rapture, with strong absorption in God and suspension of the faculties, but without loss of the senses.

In 1862 complete raptures were frequent, sometimes also with elevation from the ground, during which the spirit was illumined with ineffable knowledge and unitive embraces. When this happened in common acts, she remained still and insensible, so that no one noticed — thus she had asked of Jesus and He had promised her —; but, finding herself alone in her little room, the body was at the mercy of the intensity of the ecstasy:

«With all freedom I abandoned myself to my Good united, while outside, on the contrary, I was always distracted, I kept myself always occupied in material things and I fled the sermons too, because, from the immense greed I had for the word of God I went there, (but) I had to go away, because I always feared…; but in my room, above all at night, which I spent entirely with Him alone…» (M 1.1, pp. 21, 23f, 345) […].

In the memorable conference on the love of God of 14 March […] at the moment of Communion:

«All at once an arrow strikes her in the heart; it burns the left arm. She does not know what to do in such a state; she cannot leave. All at once she falls asleep, enjoys, rejoices, feels her God within her, sees his love, she feels the flames of the fire of her God that burn her. In such a state she no longer feels anything human; they prick her, they shake her: she is insensible; and it is such that, if God did not withdraw little by little, she would die. In the end, she… sees her God, feels him, tastes him, and at that moment her body is dead to the earth» 29.

It is proper to the ecstatic experience to lose the notion of time and space, since infused communications are not subject to perceptive or discursive succession nor to localized projection. She says so herself with precision: «Whoever is in that state has no knowledge either of the hours or of what is of the earth» (M 4,3, p. 4f). After the strong moment of rapture has passed, its effects continue for a long time, the senses remain as though drowsy, consciousness of external realities is slowly resumed, while the spirit finds it hard to free itself from the unitive intoxication. «I remained so united — she writes at Pentecost 1878, after describing an ecstasy had at night —, that all day it seemed to me I was always in the midst of what I had seen and experienced» (M 1.2, p. 1165).

Her concern to avoid others noticing appears continually; she has confidence in the promise reiterated by the Lord, and prays to Him: «My Good, when I am alone, do with me what you will, burn me, consume me, annihilate me, but let no one notice!» (M 1.1, p. 51). Often she must do herself continued violence to maintain attention to what she is doing or to what they are saying to her (M 1.2, p. 113f). But, however much she strives to attend externally and however much assurance she has in Jesus' promise, she does not always succeed in escaping the eyes of those present. One day in 1890, while she was speaking to the novices about the love of God, she was so inflamed that she was seen by them raised about a hand's breadth from the floor for the space of almost half an hour 30.

So she herself pointed out in the month of June 1885: «little or nothing do I experience of rapture, and the union with God is different» (M 5.4, p. 22) 31.

Crown of thorns - Stigmata

Christ Crucified was the center of Rosa Gattorno's spirituality and, therefore, configuration to Him, in spirit and in body, could not fail to be her supreme longing. Her preferred, daily contemplation was that of the Passion. As in the other true stigmatics, this contemplation and that conforming love disposed her to receive the gift of the bodily projection of the wounds of the Redeemer, which were already fixed in her spirit 32. Only that, according to her wish not to give occasion for admiration with extraordinary graces, she obtained from the Lord that everything be hidden: she had indeed the pain of the wounds, but not the external signs.

The sorrowful participation in the Passion of the Redeemer began shortly after her husband's death. From the testimonies of the sisters and from the Memoirs we know that Mother Rosa spent the sacred triduum — Holy Thursday, Friday and Saturday — totally withdrawn in her room and in absolute fast. But no one was witness to what the Lord made her experience in those days, until on Good Friday of 1886 Sister A. Camilla Valentini managed, by a stratagem, to enter her room in Rome: she found the Mother stretched out as on a cross, in a spasmodic agony by virtue of the pains of the crown of thorns, of the wounds of the hands and feet, of the whole body. She was able to observe closely the marks of the thorns on the forehead and, in the palms of the hands, the shape as of a hard nail of flesh. Having asked her how long such things had been happening to her, the Mother answered: «Twenty-eight years» (the witness says she did not understand well whether she meant
