And she confided to her that every Friday similar sufferings were renewed, though not with that intensity. She imposed on her, however, absolute secrecy about what she had learned on that occasion. The sister, indeed, so kept it until after the Foundress's death (FIOCCHI, II, pp. 202-204).

Among the fruits of the aforementioned novena of Our Lady of the Vineyards of 1859 one was the desire to share in the pains of the Savior's crown of thorns. One day she felt placed on her head, by two angels, the longed-for crown and experienced the pricks of the thorns: «the desire to suffer was great, the pleasure was immense — she writes —; how happy I would have been if they had left it to me forever!». She obtained from the confessor permission to fashion one and wear it on her head on the night from Friday to Saturday; but she had to stop, because one of the nights a wound remained on her forehead, which swelled, and she had to disguise it with her hair so that her family would not notice (M 1.1, p. 65).

We do not know whether the strong headache, very localized, which she mentions very often, was due to natural causes or had a mystical origin; a hint of hers on 28 December 1876 could suggest such a gift (M 4.4, p. 885).

On the other hand, the pain of the wounds in the feet, hands and side was permanent, with a more intense renewal every Friday. In 1862, during the novena of the Savior, she had «very strong pains in the hands, feet and heart». Previously to this date she had tied to her breast, on the side of the heart, a small crucifix, which she kept pressed day and night for five years, until gangrene appeared, because it had penetrated the flesh; she was ordered to remove it (M 1.1, p. 32; FIOCCHI, I, p. 45 note 5).

In the brief affective and unitive meditations of Lent 1864 the longing to share in all Jesus' sufferings is evident; in that of the 44th day she writes:

«Tell me, my Love: I think I have been able to arrive at everything to try to follow you in sufferings, but I do not know how to obtain that nails be driven into my hands and feet…» (M 2. p. 167) […].

Scholars of mystical phenomena in general, and concretely of stigmatization, today give no importance to the miraculous character or not of the bodily manifestations but to the cause that produces them. They are true stigmata, those somatic localizations or projections that originate in the infused contemplation of Christ's sufferings in the Passion, even if, as is known of some canonized saints, a volitional propensity to arrive at that loving identification with the Crucified had preceded. What counts is the sincerity of the subject who experiences it.

Ardors in the heart - Exchange of hearts

Here is the bodily phenomenon of which Mother Rosa speaks several times in the Memoirs and in the letters to Fr. Gennaro. It is not new in Christian hagiography.

The first and beautiful mention of the fires of love appears in the notes of the meditations made day by day in Lent 1864 in Genoa:

«A devouring fire came upon me, which consumed me, and there were moments when I seemed to be destroyed in that fire. I enjoyed immensely, and yet it was a terrible and very tasty agony. I felt a great and consoling pleasure at feeling myself destroyed, and I would never have wished it to cease for me. Oh! how sweet it is to die of love!» (M 2, p. 1445).

In 1866 we find a similar outpouring on the devouring fire that «makes her faint» with pain and with sweetness at the same time (M 1.1, p. 45f). In 1867 the ardor becomes ever more blazing: she feels herself burn, be consumed, it does not let her rest (M 1.1, p. 49f, 58-61). And already in 1870 she feels a swelling on the side of the heart that, often, even presses on the ribs. The pain is strong and continuous. She fears others will notice, because it assails her also in common acts and while speaking with persons. The phenomenon is repeated each time she experiences strong impulses of love toward God. Often she is forced to withdraw and shut herself in her room so as not to give occasion for admiration. At other times she needs to take cold-water baths to mitigate the ardor. It is a heartrending suffering and simultaneously a most sweet loving enjoyment, which keeps her united to her Good, and obliges her to exclaim: «Alas! my Good, you make me die!». Here is how she expresses herself in the month of October 1873:

p. 978

«The swelling of the heart was in these days without equal, the fire devoured me, destroyed me. The suffering I feel from so great a swelling is such that I cannot describe it; but much greater is the joy I feel; because this keeps me so tightly bound to my Good, no pain is a nuisance to me» (M 4.2, p. 12).

In her descriptions she speaks both of the swelling on the left side, effect of the loving ardors, and of the pain on the right side, coinciding with the renewal of the pain of the wounds of the hands and feet; it is therefore the wound of the side. In 1870 she hints at a scar, different from the one left by the small crucifix she had worn embedded in the flesh; it proceeds from a wound of the crucified Lord, which seems to want to open (M 1.2, p. 31). On the feast of Corpus Domini 1872, being in church, she felt a sharp blow in the breast as of a stylus piercing her (M 3, p. 438); the pain of this wound became unbearable at certain moments. She writes in February 1873:

«Today, more than usual, the right side tormented me and was much more swollen; and that burning I feel within, which burns me in a single point, as if I had a wound: it is not heat, no, a burning like a wound which, when it comes strong, I feel myself even faint. And I see well that they notice, because they tell me I change color…» (M 4.1, p. 335).

On 16 January 1875 she speaks again of the small scar; the pain she feels is «as of a thin knife being thrust into her» (M 4,3, p. 12).

When she put herself under the direction of Fr. Gennaro Granito di Belmonte, at first she was ashamed to disclose to him what happened in her heart. In one of the letters she tells him that, by now, «the swelling is quite stationary…; it grows at night; I no longer have those exertions (strains)…». On the other hand she feels that her breath fails; and she is assailed by «the fear that it may be a» cardiac illness, effect of the violent ardors of past years (L undated, no. 347).

Among the various mystical experiences in relation to the heart is that of the exchange or interchange of hearts, of which there are many cases in hagiography. It consists in the persuasion that one's own heart has been replaced by that of the Lord, so that the mystic feels she loves Him with her own divine-human heart. This gift too Rosa Gattorno seems to hint at on various dates, although she has not left us an explicit account of the fact, which occurred at the beginning of her gift of herself to the Lord, it seems. So she recalls it on the feast of the Name of Mary 1870:

«Abandoned, I threw myself on the Side of my Good, where many years ago He took my heart, which was within this miserable breast, and so in Him I remained that, on coming to myself, I was left full of peace and comfort» (M 1.1, p. 82).

In 1876 and 1877, and again in 1890, she says several times while speaking with the Lord: «This heart of yours, which is swollen»; or notes: «the part where his heart is» (M 4.4, pp. 14, 19, 26, 44, 103; 4.5, p. 21f; 11.2, p. 269).

Both in this experience and in the others concerning the heart it seems that Rosa Gattorno had before her no model of imitation in the life and writings of any saint. She lived it all in her chosen isolation, carefully protected from the gaze of others: a spousal love kindled, suffered and enjoyed in the most jealous intimacy.

4. The part of the devil

The masters of the ways of the spirit have always warned souls against the snares of Satan, bearing in mind that this counterfeiter of the works of God often «disguises himself as an angel of light» (2 Cor 11:14). They distinguish diabolical temptation, that is, the enemy's interior insinuations, from diabolical obsession, which can act both on the interior faculties, by means of fixed ideas, scruples, fears, images, and on the external senses, through apparitions, representations, voices, noises, blows… There will hardly be a mystic who has not had to do with diabolical vexations; let us recall, among the best-known saints, Anthony the abbot, Francis of Assisi, Catherine of Siena, Margaret of Cortona, Teresa of Avila, Francis Xavier, Veronica Giuliani, John Mary Vianney, Gemma Galgani.

It should not cause wonder that Satan launches his attacks in a particular way against the great friends of God and, still more fiercely, against those who, like the apostles of the Gospel and the founders of religious institutes, are valid instruments of the growth of the Kingdom. But we must not attribute to him more room than God permits him to take. If it is difficult, as was said above, to draw a dividing line between the sphere of God's action and that of human elaboration in the supernatural process, still more difficult is it to discover the presence of the devil and to distinguish between his malign arts and the imaginative and sensory creativity of the subject.

There are persons, even psychically healthy, particularly prone to interior apprehensions and figurative fantasies. Those moreover accustomed to see their own and others' vicissitudes in the perspective of faith tend to group the human race into good and bad, those who are on God's side and those who are on the devil's side. Persuaded that they are doing God's part and are his instruments, they easily feel hindered and persecuted by the forces of evil, and see in every contradictor a mandatary or collaborator of Satan; they discover everywhere plots and trickeries of the powers of darkness.

Rosa Gattorno recognized herself as inclined to apprehensions, that is, temperamentally led to nourish within herself fears and disturbances, which could nest and take shape in her fantasy. St. John of the Cross insistently warns against the danger of abetting the action of the enemy, who makes use of the subject's suggestions and imagination to disquiet her spirit.

I must confess that the only thing I would have preferred not to find in the Memoirs of Rosa Gattorno is this tedious succession of diabolical irruptions, almost every night, by means of grotesque figures; and then that seeing always the shadow of Cepinello, as she humorously calls him, in every difficulty and every displeasure arising from the normal vicissitudes of the foundation.

At the beginning of her new life, in the years 1858-1862, she had to endure violent temptations and anxieties of conscience, especially regarding the Eucharist, the penances undertaken, the confessions made. The struggle reached such a point that her director, Fr. Giuseppe Firpo, wished to have recourse to exorcisms, as if it were a true obsession, which Rosa refused to accept, as was said above. In reality it was nothing other than one of those trials of passive purification that accompany every radical renunciation in order to give oneself to God; moreover, it belonged to her special vocation to the following of the suffering Christ.

In the following years temptations against faith appeared, and those of despair, true diabolical suggestions accompanied by frightening apparitions. So in the novena of the Immaculate Conception of 1866 (M 1.1, p. 45). The temptations were of every sort, except those against purity, «from which, by God's mercy, I have always been free», she repeats several times.

In November 1874 the tempter tormented her for several days with the obsession of going mad, making her see signs of madness in her own way of behaving. The temptation of despair was added, with impulses to throw herself from the window (M 1.1, p. 75; 12, p. 51-55, 58f, 77-79, 84, 86).

The interior temptations were accompanied by external spites, noises, blows and commotions, which at the beginning, Rosa being still in Genoa, were heard from outside (M 1.1, p. 555). There were added the apparitions of monstrous figures which, in the little room at Piacenza, were repeated every night. Deformed beasts, black shadows in the shape of big spiders «with long legs and little body», climbing along the wall or attached to the ceiling; then they vanished. Strong jolts that woke her; invisible hands that removed the straw of the bed and scratched the blanket over her feet…

From the descriptions she gives of these phantoms and from the fact that she always sees them after lying down, in a supine position, they suggest those sensory figurations of the half-sleep, frequent in persons of sound mind, but which have nothing preternatural about them, except the effect they can produce. In Mother Rosa's spirit they left greater courage to overcome difficulties and a renewed desire to work in the service of God.

Certainly, a prudent director could have helped her to overcome that persecution simply by reducing the phenomenon to its reality; but she found herself alone; no one knew of that continued battle until she confided in her two spiritual friends of the last years: the Princess of Fitalia, whom she jokingly informed of the ridiculous apparitions that disturbed her, and Fr. Gennaro Granito di Belmonte, her director. He gave her as a remedy to command those monsters to leave her in peace, since «obedience does not want her rest to be disturbed»; the method had some effect, at least regarding interior peace, although the disturbances continued. Six months later she wrote to him humorously:

«As to my spirit I am most tranquil. The passage continues: good ones and bad ones came; visits I had many. One sees they find pleasure in traveling, especially at night and, though it is poor and almost uninhabited, my poor room evidently pleases, is it not so?» (L 2.1.1889, 8.6.1889).

IV. LOVE AND SUFFERING: THE MISSION OF A LIFE

The heart of Rosa Gattorno, a woman's heart, endowed with a rich sensibility and an exceptional capacity for welcome and affective self-giving, was made to love. And it was also a heart made to suffer. Suffering enters into the Christian logic of oblative and redemptive love, since God's love for us was manifested in the fact that He sent his Son as an expiatory victim for our sins (1 Jn 4:9f); and the Son of God demonstrated his love for the Father and for men by submitting to the passion and death on the cross.

It is not only a matter of Mother Rosa's personal spirituality: to love and to suffer will also be her destiny as foundress and will constitute her central message to the Daughters of St. Anne. In the poem Labors and Consolations she presents the growth of the Institute as the laborious rowing of a little ship through the storms of the sea, until, after a great struggle, it is seen to emerge victorious unfurling an elegant flag with the inscription: suffering-love. With favorable sea, the ship, grown very large and well equipped, makes great progress, defends itself successfully against enemies, now strongly armored and girded with iron; it keeps gaining ground, conquers many cities and countries. «Always victorious it betakes itself to great ports and flies its flags: suffering and love» (TC, pp. 219-221).

1. «Love, and do what you will» (St. Augustine) Whoever loves father or mother, son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me (Mt 10:37)

Rosa experienced in all its force having to renounce the most sacred human affections by virtue of God's preferential love. First of all her own parents, whom she loved deeply and by whom she was deeply loved. After her choice of consecrated life, at the moment of leaving for Piacenza to begin the Work of God, she did not hesitate to accept for herself and for them the painful separation; on 13 March 1866, mastering the anguish of her heart, she had the courage to step over the body of her mother, seated on the threshold of the house door (FIOCCHI, I, p. 1205). Sixteen years later she also had the strength to leave that same mother dying, because her presence was urgently required by the sisters of the community of Pisa (Memoirs of Mother Celsa, 1882). In a dream, had in 1896, she will see her in heaven dressed as a daughter of St. Anne.

She loved her brothers and sisters. We know of her good relations with Francesco, who later would testify at the informative process in Genoa, as also with her sister Elisa. No less was her affection toward her brother Federico: despite his ideological distance, she had great understanding toward him and he reciprocated with the same love, almost veneration.

But the great sacrifice was the separation from her children. The pain felt when she lost the third of them, Francesco, ten months old, she would feel renewed many years later. On 24 August 1874 she seemed to hear still his voice calling her: «Mama, mama!» (M 1.2, p. 47). With Carlotta, the deaf-mute daughter, she took care to place her in the Institute for the Deaf-Mutes of Milan, so that, learning to speak, she might then be suitably placed in society; while little Alessandro, who gave signs of priestly vocation, she entrusted to a private school to prepare him for ecclesiastical studies. But the moment of the terrible alternative arrived: having to choose between maternal duties and God's design. She described that painful juncture dramatically:

«My children! the mere thought of having to leave them was an anguish, and I repeated to myself: No! it will never be, no! And the good Shepherd (the archbishop) granted me to go to Rome… It seemed to me that I had already won the victory: never — I kept repeating to myself — will Pope Pius IX permit a mother to leave her children, a mother who bore them an exceeding affection…».

But the answer of Pius IX, in the private audience of 3 January […] in his work!» (M 2, pp. 11, 16-18, 24-26).

Those words of the Vicar of Christ, which she always considered inspired by God, quieted her and gave her the courage to go forward. Very often, in the not always pleasant vicissitudes of the lives of the two sons, a kind of remorse will assail her, but she will always hear resounding in her conscience the answer of Pius IX.

The attention to the Work did not prevent her from taking care of her children with solicitous love. She maintained with them constant communication, especially with Alessandro, who made her suffer so much, until she had the consolation of seeing him converted and of assisting him in his last illness. The grief at his death was immense; but she had promised the Lord not to weep if she saw him die as a Christian, and she fulfilled her promise 33.

She had known how to raise natural maternal affection to the plane of evangelical charity, which is universal. So she expressed herself in 1872:

«I had a most beautiful lesson on how I must love my neighbor, and this also regarding my children. How I must conduct myself and the perfect equality with which I must treat all creatures and love them all in Him and for Him. Give to creatures as much as was given to me, to save them and lead them to love and serve Him. Oh! incomprehensible Love of mine, what I felt!» (M 1.1, p. 1085).

With the sisters she was demanding in renunciation of one's own family, but she taught them not to stifle legitimate affections toward their own relatives; she did not like coldness in relations with them. She wrote in 1873 to Sister A. Carlotta Biagini:

«Listen, my beloved: I would like you to write to your mother and so two lines to Signora Maria, but truly all honey I would want them to be, and you to tell her so many beautiful consoling words about your state that you have embraced, the consolation you feel… You will give her your address, telling her that you wish to be often blessed by your mother» (L 29-10-1873) […].

2. The mysticism of suffering Rosa Gattorno belongs to the ranks of so many great lovers

33 On the maternal concern and the sufferings because of the two sons cf. A.M. FIOCCHI, II, pp. 119-144. who, like St. Teresa of Avila, St. John of the Cross, St. M. Magdalene de' Pazzi, St. Veronica Giuliani, made of suffering, so to speak, the why of their existence: a mission, that is, of completing the sufferings of Christ (cf. Col 1:24), collaborating in his redemptive immolation.

In such a mission suffering is inseparable from love: love is the cause of suffering, suffering is the expression of love. In Mother Rosa's Memoirs one passes constantly from heartrending pages, where she lays bare her sufferings of spirit — darkness, abandonments by God, temptations of despair — to others in which we see her enjoy intimate loving union with the Beloved, or experience the impetuous fires that oblige her to cry out: «Love, you make me die!». The same cry of pain-love her heart exhales when she experiences the shudders caused by the interior wounds of the hands, feet and side or by the chain embedded in the flesh.

It was in the process of mystical purification, at the beginning of her widowhood, that she made the discovery of the treasure of suffering. Beautifully she recalls it, in her allegorical language, in the exordium of the book Labors and Consolations:

«… My Crucified taught me to suffer and, like the honey of bees, enclosed in those precious combs, preserved suffering for me, which changed into sweetness. From time to time He gave me of this humor to taste and, with sublime lessons, made me understand how so much exquisiteness was drawn from suffering, while nature was rebellious to it…

My Crucified left me alone and, like the bride of the Canticles, I went wandering in that forest to seek Him, taking a step forward on the path and another back. All the little branches were dry and all interwoven as signs of crosses.

— Do you too join my sadness? — I went saying to them.

Stopping, my Crucified placed on my shoulders his heavy cross and, having removed from me the terror of suffering, left me an ardent love for it. Much have I loved it and I love it greatly» (TC, p. 3-5).

In her first impulses of love she would have wished to immolate herself radically, all at one stroke, through martyrdom. On 31 March 1862, after a vision of the Host dripping with blood, she had «a most lively, most ardent desire to suffer martyrdom for the faith; and, to be able to give vent to this thought of mine — she writes —, how many things did I not think of to be able to succeed! My Good! I would not be satisfied unless I have the fortune to see myself ground to pieces for you, dear Beloved!» (M 1.1, p. 245). […]

To live to suffer! will be her answer every time the desire for death offers itself to her spirit as the means of freeing herself from the prison of the body and flying to the supreme Good.

Carrying the cross with Jesus

The Christian's suffering, according to Jesus' invitation (Mt 10:38; Lk 9:23; 14:27) and the theology of St. Paul (Gal 2:19; 6:14), has a name: the Cross. And it is the name preferred by Mother Rosa. She confesses that still in 1859, made greedy by the great consolations of those beginnings, she was not accustomed to «fight under the standard of the holy Cross, delightful and dear». She was a «beginner» (M 1.1, p. 4). But she was not slow to enter fully into the school of the Cross: this will always be her «companion», her «bed of rest» (M. 3, p. 25). One day when she was full of bitterness, holding the cross very tightly, she spoke thus with it: «Is it true, my treasure, that you are always my companion?». And she heard a voice that comforted her: «Only from the Cross does one learn to love!» (TC, p. 329).

Not content with constantly having the image of the Crucified before the eyes of the body and of the spirit, she wished to make her love sensible by tying a small cross tightly to her breast, taking her brief rest lying on a cross and often remaining hung on a large wooden cross that she had in her little room at Piacenza. But it was the mystery itself of the Cross, more than the materiality of it, that had configured her life.

And she would have wished each of the daughters of St. Anne to become a true lover of the Cross. Encouragements in this sense are very frequent in her letters; here are some:

«Courage on the way of Calvary, if you wish to be crucified with your Beloved and to die with Him on the delightful bed of the Cross» - «Every new day, a new cross! Blessed is the one whose dawn breaks amid thorns and sorrows!» - «In paradise there is no more cross, there are no more sufferings there: only Love, Love… Cheer up, cheer up, for Jesus likes those who suffer: whoever does not want to suffer does not want to love!» - «Whoever wishes to follow me — says the Master showing us a cross —, let him take up his cross and follow me. Well then, what language is this, heavenly Spouse? O blessed souls! He gives me that treasure which the world does not know and which He offers to his beloved brides, and indeed seeks that it be heavy, so that one may come one day to taste his delights» - «This holy Wood, nuptial bed of his most beloved brides!» (L to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 27-5-1869, 1-1-1870; to Sr. Adelaide Pezzoni: 1869, 16-1-1870; to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino: 23-12-1868, 6-2-1870).

On 27 July 1890 she had a special light on the three degrees of the cross or three ways of carrying the cross, and on this subject she gave many other conferences to the sisters. The first degree is that of the religious who carry it on their shoulders for love of God, but always complaining and seeking comfort from the superior, from the confessor… The second degree: those who carry it pressed to the breast, never lay it down, find happiness in it and are generous in suffering. The third degree: the true lovers of the Lord, who know no other comfort than suffering; they carry the cross pressed to the breast and seek to suck from it the wormwood, the essence of suffering, without seeking the slightest comfort: «only suffering is their refreshment; only at the feet of the Lord do they weep and secretly shed their tears and pressed to the heart they hold the holy cross, love of the seraphim, joy of those who love! These are the holy souls». And she concluded:

«O my Love; how much I too desire to love and to be able to learn and possess this holy cross!… Ah! sweet Love! whoever does not love you is too unfortunate. How happy I would be if I could make everyone know you and love you! Poor creatures» (M 10.4, p. 3f; 11.2, pp. 318-325) […].

3. Sufferings of every sort

Reading Rosa Gattorno's notes we feel almost led to number her among those persons, especially women, who see life as a true «valley of tears» and find their own identity, so to speak, in suffering sought and cultivated. A sweet pessimism envelops their intimate feelings and their communication with others. But Rosa Gattorno is anything but a pessimistic woman; deeply joyful, she spreads courage and the will to live around her. She discovers, yes, in every circumstance the hurtful side of her sensibility; but she accepts it with faith, because she knows that pain is an essential part of her destiny. She wrote in 1872 to Fr. Agostino Donadio:

«I am immensely suffering, I do not know where to take breath, the weight of afflictions suffocates me and takes away my strength, my poor brain is a mouth of Vesuvius, because into it plunge the great tumults of every kind. One thing alone is my support: the will of God».

Bodily ailments

She never had robust health. She herself speaks of faintings caused by weakness, of attacks of fever, of strong headaches, of stomach disorders, of swelling, of irregular pulse… The sisters who accompanied her on journeys were witnesses of the fatigue these cost her, of the sufferings she did not always manage to conceal. The doctors, however, could never ascertain what her ailments concretely were, because she did not submit to any visit or inspection, not wishing to show the instruments of penance and their marks.

Moreover, both her diet and the terrible bodily macerations contributed to a permanent weakening and endangered, often gravely, her health, producing intolerable spasms. Add the pain of the hidden stigmata and, above all, that of the inflammation of the heart, which left her without strength. And then the exhausting work of every day. Such a way of living cannot be understood without a special divine assistance.

How did Mother Rosa bear her ailments? First of all by not allowing them to rule her existence: they did not make her slow the rhythm of her activity or renounce her journeys in service of the Work of God, still less did they exempt her from common observances. In her letters she often alludes, rather in a humorous tone, to her illnesses. From those written to Mons. Granito di Belmonte, her spiritual Father, one glimpses what her spiritual attitude was regarding bodily ailments:

«This donkey is so worn out that she cannot stand on her feet: a slow little fever I feel consumes my bones, I am swollen like a balloon. What a pain! But everything is little for Jesus… Here I am, with head bowed I adore his designs. I suffer much, ah! but, like the hedgehog, I stay curled up at the feet of my dear Crucified (17-8-1885) - «It is very sweet to be accompanied by so continual a pain. Every now and then I am obliged to apply the linseed poultice, to relieve the spasm, for I had never experienced neuralgic pains… My God! there are moments when it is stronger than my strength and I feel myself failing. But resigned to God's will, how calmly I savor it all!» (17-5-1888) […].

Sufferings of the spirit

Endowed with great sensibility, she could not remain indifferent to the situations of others, especially when they were persons to whom she felt more bound. We recall her sufferings because of her children and her brother Federico. Nothing afflicted her like the sense of the offense against God. She wrote in 1890 to her friend the Princess of Fitalia:

«Dear Emilia, I feel my breast breaking with sorrow, thinking how dear Jesus is offended and by whom He is offended. I do not know what I would do; I feel a courage that, were it not for God, our sweet Love, where I would go I do not know. Let us leave it, and pray strongly» (28-5-1890).

For one who loves God, in fact, the evil of evils is sin. Rosa Gattorno wept all her life over what, in her humility, she called «my great sins», «my wickednesses», not because she doubted God's pardon, but precisely because she felt so lovingly embraced by the mercy of the supreme Love. The mere thought that she could still offend Him tortured her atrociously.

It is well known among connoisseurs of spirituality that one of the most effective means of purification is the struggle against temptations, of which the most terrible are those concerning the foundation of faith and trust in God. Sometimes they are true diabolical obsessions, at other times simple obscurations that fix themselves tenaciously in the interior faculties in the form of scruples, fears, anguish and despair. The torment of the spirit reaches its peak when the soul feels it has lost its God forever, seeing itself irremissibly damned.

God did not spare Rosa Gattorno this price of the victory of Love, common to almost all the great mystics. She often speaks of the most subtle temptations with which the enemy pursues her; only she feels specially protected, by special grace of God, against impure suggestions.

Now she feels rejected by God, convinced that her communions are sacrilegious (M 4.2, p. 4f); now the tempter persuades her that everything she experiences is «false and diabolical art, effect of human sensibility» (M 4.3, p. 10f); now he makes her see that her life is nothing but «an abyss of wickedness», which have led her to certain damnation (M 4.2, pp. 61-63; lett. to Fr. Donadio: 9-10-1872). Often she is assailed by the obsessive fear of going mad, indeed it seems to her she already is, because everything is done by her «without judgment, as by one who is not in her right mind» (M 4.3, pp. 555, 65; 4.4, p. 1085; 5.4, p. 278).

In the years 1875-1877 she was the victim of most ferocious temptations of despair that drove her mad. On 29 May 1875, being at Torricella, she left written:

«Strong agitation. It seemed to me my nature was changing and that I would go mad from one minute to the next… What I feel suggested to me is horrendous, as if it were already so: Behold, you will do this and that. Do you see that you are no longer in reason, do you see that you will have to throw yourself out of the window? Ah! resist, but in a moment you will no longer be able to resist…» (M 4.3, p. 635).

This almost obsessive impulse to throw herself out of the window returns constantly in those years, always during the night. Sometimes she feels physically pushed by the tempter, dragged to the windowsill, and always threatened: «I will throw you out of the window!» (cf. M 4.3, pp. 21-26, 70-75; 4.4, pp. 1-13, 46, 49f, 52f, 125). On 23 February she summed up the pitiless struggle thus:

«The fierce one has for some time taken up diabolical suggestions, which are always the same: that he throws me out of the window already, that he kills me, that he will make me lose my head and I shall be left an idiot, that my end will be despair, because I live in sin and always renew the sacrileges: without ever, however, pointing one out to me. In short the tumult he puts in my poor mind is such as to be unbelievable» (M 4.4, p. 36).

The battle culminated in the month of April 1877 with very strong temptations of suicide (M 4.4, p. 139).

It will seem inconceivable that such a situation, continued for months and years, can enter into God's design, not even as permission, and that it can coexist with the heroic exercise of hope, indeed with the trusting intimacy of unitive love. But it is a more than frequent fact in the history of Christian hagiography. Mother Rosa, at the end of the most piteous descriptions, adds from time to time observations like these: «Although I am in the midst of an abyss of pains, yet a something keeps me within a peace that is indescribable». «In offering Him such miserable pains, He makes me feel an inner peace unspeakable» (M 4.4, pp. 89, 105).

The soul emerges from these combats purified and strengthened in faith and hope, disabused of itself, humbled, and stronger in fidelity to Love. Mother Rosa does not doubt that God will prevail in her, but she suffers thinking of third parties who may be victims. In 1889 she confided in Mons. Granito di Belmonte:

«It is always an ugly thing to fight with an enemy who hates me, and I more than she: I feel a something, we are always at fisticuffs! Those who suffer from it are those poor creatures who find themselves in the middle… - I am always in the midst of the struggles. It is true that victory is also sure for me, but the cannonades always wound and strike on the open wounds, because there is no time to be able to heal them» (3-5-1889, 29-8-1889).

With temptations are joined those other intimate sufferings, which are part of the great and supreme purification, known under the name of night of the spirit, a true purgatory in life: aridity, abandonments, distance from God. These are torments that only one can understand who, after having experienced the ineffable sweetness of loving union with God, sees himself deprived of so great a good, without the possibility any longer of placing his love in anything other than Him. This pain of love, which surpasses every other, has inspired the most sublime pages of the mystics of all times; we find them very frequent in Mother Rosa's spiritual diary.

The first experience of aridity, effect of the passage to infused contemplation, occurs when, as St. John of the Cross teaches, the soul feels invaded by God and the lower faculties — senses, imagination, intellect — remain suspended, without object, while the will, an eminently arid faculty, is drawn by God with force. In one of the first pages, so beautifully autobiographical, of the book Labors and Consolations, Mother Rosa recalls with precision such an experience at the beginning of her mystical ascents:

«My Crucified left me in the dark, off the path, without intellect, unable to reason. Everything was closed, the night was horrid and dark, and I could not understand where I was. I would have wished to reason but, as I said, this faculty was taken from me, and not even the comfort of weeping was given me» (TC, p. 6).

This probably happened in 1859, on the eve of the Most Holy Redeemer, as she relates at the beginning of her Memoirs:

«While I expected great consolations, because I was used to having them, especially on solemnities, instead I found myself arid. Alas! how will it be? Perhaps it is I who have committed something and so my Good has gone from me. What have I done? And I was very upset; I did not know where to find peace…» […].

More terrible than simple aridity is the state of abandonment, in which the soul feels as if left definitively by God, finds all roads closed, sees itself as in a dark prison without a ray of light. The Servant of God has described with heartrending accents, a hundred times, this torment, equivalent to the pain of loss in purgatory and in hell. Let this page of 1874 serve as an example:

«The pain I feel is too much… Alas, I fell into terrible temptation of despair: the pain of having been able to displease the Being of my life and that, for this, my Love had unhappily abandoned me! Pain without equal! I was in agony. Oh! with what sword my breast was pierced! I called Him, I asked His pardon, but nothing!… The soul writhed. The pains that came upon me were of every kind, so that I fainted. Having come to, my word was:

— I have lost my God!

Three days in so painful a state I stayed: never again shall I be able to forget them. On the fourth, as soon as I had made holy Communion, a sweet voice said to me:

— Rosa, how much you have made me suffer! — I heard the voice of my Beloved.

Alas! unfortunately it is true. Pardon! what have I done?…

I remained I know not how to say, because one has to experience it to know what it is. What a pain it was! But in ecstasy I remained… Meanwhile the soul was cleared of so dense a cloud and resumed its first state: peace and resignation in adversity… Having come to, I realized I was another…» (M 1.1, p. 166f).

Usually this is the end of every situation of distance from God, which often is prolonged for several days: the meeting with the beloved Good, who makes her feel the tenderness of his love, fully compensates her for the pains suffered. Through the Memoirs one can observe the process of the victories of pure faith in those secret tortures that, for many years, had no other witness nor other confidant than the pages of the notebook of notes.

That entering into the night of the spirit has as its fruit the total purification, which opens the way to pure love. Often she has the sensation of being damned, it seems to her she experiences true pains of hell; and it is precisely at that moment that her heart exhales the most moving outpourings of love:

«The poor soul, amid the despair of the damned, finds it has lost its Being. It does not find Him anywhere. Yes, my God! I go to the tabernacle, and as mute I find myself…; wherever I turn I see nothing but a precipice; I cast a glance at my actions, to see whether in them I could find something that might comfort me…, ever more I see myself destitute, nothing can I see of having: everything remains dissipated in the presence of my nothingness. What pains these are! I do not speak of the fear this state causes: I can only say that these are the pains of hell. I have lost my Beloved, sole object of my living!» (M 3, p. 278) […].

External tribulations: obstacles and contradictions

Setbacks, misunderstandings, persecutions are the normal patrimony of all who commit themselves to the following of Christ. The life of Rosa Gattorno could not be an exception. Since she accepted, by God's will, her mission as foundress she understood that it is the mark of every evangelical enterprise to have to face, first of all, the postulates of human prudence and then the opposition, not only of the enemies of the interests of the Kingdom, but also of the good and well-intentioned who do not share or do not understand the viewpoints of one who acts under divine impulse.

She had the consciousness of being an instrument of God, though unskilled: her foundation was the Work of God. It is no wonder if in every contradictor she saw an adversary of God's design, indeed an unconscious collaborator of the evil one. Hence her deep suffering, especially when she discovered in opponents hypocrisy, ulterior motives and hidden personal interests. Let us not forget then her tendency to convert every unforeseen event into a motive and opportunity for suffering. In reality it fell to her to bear true calumnies, all the more painful as they came from persons to whom she had given trust, affection and sacrifice (cf. FIOCCHI, I, pp. 1815, 186-189, 199-220); or from those whom she venerated deeply as ministers of the Church.

It is not the place to list the manifold occasions that embittered and purified her spirit, already so troubled by interior pains. We shall limit ourselves to hinting at her sentiments in the face of such situations.

At the beginning of her Memoirs she wrote, recalling the year 1858:

«The family tribulations were without equal; but, always pressed to my Good, I went on repeating: Oh! my sins deserve worse and hell itself…» (M 1.1, p. 25).

Her own account of what happened at Piacenza on 31 March 1869 because of the calumnious accusations raised by the superior of the house herself, is the best testimony of her behavior in similar cases and, above all, of her ready and generous pardon (M 1.2, pp. 21-28).

After summarizing the five persecutions suffered in the years 1868 and 1869, «a firework from all sides», she adds:

«Only one thing comforts me, and it is that no rancor has ever remained in me toward whoever caused me so many pains and whoever it was, indeed I feel toward them a very great affection and for them I have increased my prayers, and I always tried to do them whatever good I could» (M 1.2, pp. 28-31).

And here too one of those sincerest introspections of hers surprises us. One day the suspicion came to her that her aforesaid tendency led her to discover malice where there was none and to magnify the causes of suffering out of a certain secret enjoyment in suffering; Jesus gave her the answer:

«My beloved, everything that is done to you, I receive the same pain: your pains are mine. You want to know why you suffer so much pain at seeing your daughters and those you keep near you act so maliciously? Be calm, for there is nothing human in it; but since everything that offends me you must feel painfully, so you feel more than appears» (M 1.1, p. 1695).

The thought that Jesus suffers with her, indeed that behind the misunderstandings and obstacles she meets He is always there to sustain her and help her fight, instills courage and security in her. In the month of May 1872, amid terrible sufferings because of the difficulties met in getting the Rules approved, she wrote:

«How sweet it is to live in Jesus, resigned to the will of God! Today pains of one kind, tomorrow of another, today a cross with points, tomorrow with nails. All these are planted there by Jesus! Surely, if this dear Love will plant in us blades of narrow edges, yet He (will give) the strength to receive the wounds and will not permit us to remain beneath. And, if this were to happen, we shall always be happy to have been victims for our Beloved» (M 3, p. 44).

As in the other sufferings, so in external tribulations too she continually experiences the Lord's consolations and the joy of finding a way to unite herself with Him in suffering. She often exclaims: «O sweet suffering, that gives life to those who love!» (M 4.5, p. 130). «Tribulations are treasures that bring great victories» (L to Fr. Celsa Speranza: 27-8-1880). […]

4. Completing in one's own flesh the sufferings of Christ (cf. Col 1:24) The why of Rosa Gattorno's penances

Bodily mortification, in one form or another, is a constant of the whole history of Christian asceticism, indeed it is inherent in any spiritual tension also in other religions. The motivations can be various, as various are the interpretations that such a phenomenon arouses from the anthropological point of view. Certainly, there can be deviations that have nothing to do with the religious relationship with God, such as: Manichean hatred of one's own body, masochistic satisfaction, fanaticism, delirium of self-destruction, pharisaic exhibitionism… But the traditional exercise of works of penance has its root in the evangelical metanoia, which is a permanent tension of conversion and, therefore, of asceticism and renunciation, as a condition of following Christ (cf. Mt 16:24), as reparation for one's own sins, renewed struggle against one's own disordered tendencies until gaining mastery over them (cf. 1 Cor 9:27), keeping the spirit free and ready for the Lord's call…

But, from the theological point of view, there is a deeper justification: to share in the mystery of the suffering Christ, of redemptive pain, offering the Savior almost a supplement of voluntary suffering, so that He may continue his victimal immolation to the glory of the Father. Many great penitents have made their own the motivation of St. Paul: I rejoice in the sufferings I bear for you, and I complete, in my flesh, what is lacking in the sufferings of Christ, for the sake of his body, which is the Church (Col 1:24).

All this together constitutes the why of the atrocious and, let us say, exaggerated penances of Rosa Gattorno, who lived in a historical epoch in which the asceticism of relentlessness against one's own body seemed to have been surpassed. She herself was conscious of having committed herself to a style of life that was out of context; this was the main cause of not confiding in a spiritual Father for many years, convinced as she was that she would not find anyone who would approve that daily «butchery» of her members. Add that almost humble modesty of hers by which she always kept hidden from human eyes the instruments of penance and the place where she used them.

I would not exclude, as a starting point of her craving for macerations, a certain reaction against her own body or, better, against a past of compliance with natural allurements. Let us not forget that she always defined herself as a convert, with a debt to settle with the Lord. Only in such a context can the frequent insults make sense with which she vents her aversion to the body, calling it «beast of burden», «donkey», «pig», «miserable beast», and that kind of enjoyment in keeping it subdued and tortured. She sees in it as the instrument of her offenses and infidelities against the beloved Good. Logically, there is added the felt need to make reparation for herself and for others. From time to time we find invectives like this:

«I always hated you, oh infamous donkey of mine! and now I do not know what I would do to you. You, yes, you will be and were my enemy, the one who took me away from Jesus!» (M 3, p. 47).

p. 997

But the true why is nothing other than the debt of love toward the crucified Savior, from whom every redemptive sacrifice receives origin and value. She recalls how the craving for bodily penances began, in 1858:

«I took the cord of St. Francis of Assisi and (there came to me) great desire to afflict this miserable beast of a body. Had it been permitted me I would have made a butchery: so much did I hate it for having been so infamous» (M 1.1, p. 15).

With time the feeling of hatred against the body went diminishing: she rejoiced in the sufferings she procured for it, but regarded it as a good instrument of gain for the soul:

«O suffering, that I feel kill my flesh, but just as beautiful you make my soul! If once I hated this rottenness of a body, now, for what I feel that through it the soul gains, I want it less badly, and I would say that sometimes I feel moved to pity» (M 4.2, p. 86).

At certain moments she had recourse to penances to give vent to love and also to counterbalance the sufferings of the spirit (cf. M 4.5, p. 59); or simply to satisfy her insatiable thirst for suffering. Often her penances have as their aim to give efficacy to the prayer of petition for her own needs, for the needs of others, for sinners, for the souls in purgatory, for the Church (M 1.2, p. 118).

But the relationship with the life and passion of the Redeemer always returns; from each suffering of hers she takes motive to mortify taste and every satisfaction, as also to invent new forms of penance. She would have wished to make of her body a true image of that of the beloved Crucified.

From time to time she felt the need to give her penances a purpose, precisely to avoid the danger of considering them ends in themselves. One day in 1872 it was the Lord, her «director», who indicated to her with what intention she should practice some of them: «fasting for the conversion of sinners, eating herbs for the providence of the Institute, the chains so that, chained, pressed to his Heart and to his love, I may consume the wounds I bear from them, and they may help me to arrive soon at the most perfect union with you, O my eternal All» (M 3, p. 26).

In the days of Carnival 1876 she doubled her disciplines to the point of blood, and poured out her heart to Jesus:

«Ah! if only my blood in these days, when your Heart receives so many wounds from such ugly revelries — how many sins, alas, my Good! — oh! if only I had so much blood to pour out for all!…» (M 4.4, p. 375).

Mother Rosa's penitential regimen

Among the manuscripts of the Servant of God there is one in which, out of obedience, she describes retrospectively the whole unheard-of variety of penances she imposed on herself as a program from the very beginning of her gift of herself to God 34.

Already in 1856, at 25 years of age, she had bound herself by vow to perpetual fasting: a single meal a day and always meatless. She observed it rigorously until death. She had also made a vow to Our Lady not to eat fruit (M 1.2, p. 42).

In 1858, after her husband's death, she ordered bodily macerations at her pleasure. Her rest was only two hours, and this leaning on a table or on the floor. She forbade herself heating during the winter, until in 1876, following a serious pleurisy, it was necessary for her to accept the relief of a little warmth. She put chickpeas in her shoes to feel discomfort in walking.

In 1859, with the confessor's authorization, she girded herself with a leather bodice all bristling with iron points; with similar devices she also bound her legs and arms. On her breast she wore a small crucifix, which remained embedded in the flesh for five years, as said above.

But her peculiar invention was the chain of thick iron wire, with double interlocked links, girded around the waist and tightened so that she could no longer remove it. Thus she wore it for over forty years; it had sunk into the flesh, producing unbearable spasms; she had it removed three days before dying. Over this chain she placed another, thicker, which she wore tight on the flesh.

Since she enrolled in the Franciscan Third Order she wore, under her clothes, day and night, a coarse habit with the cord.

«It is three months that I have had two irons tight on my arms and they have become so embedded inside that they give me atrocious spasms. Oh! what pain! Every movement is a new torment; keeping the arm resting to write, what I feel, my Love!.. I did not have the courage to take them off. What to do? Ask someone? Oh! rather die! From 1877 she often complains of no longer being able to find even the satisfaction of shedding blood in the bloody discipline of every evening: «However much I scourge myself, very little comes out. My Good, I am miserable, I have nothing more to give you, I do not even have blood any more: this pig drags so much water that it weighs on me not a little» (M 5.1, p. 815).

On 8 December 1887, authorized by her confessor, she took heart again for a more rigorous program of penances:

«I will do the discipline to blood every evening, I will tighten the chain I wear more, so that it enters well into the flesh, the usual fast and abstinence, which I cannot increase further except by eating only bread — I would give to be seen and suspected, no! — I will have the arms well supplied with hair-shirts, I will sleep badly and little, I will work much… But I am worn out: age and the continual pains…» (M 9.2, p. 3-5).

In the last years, by command of her director Fr. Gennaro, she had to reduce the forms of penance, keeping only the chain, and moderate somewhat her rigorous diet.

On journeys, and then after the transfer of the generalate seat to Rome, she missed her little room at Piacenza, that hermitage of hers, where she could abandon herself freely, without human witnesses, to her macerations, sleeping on the wooden cross with a thick chain for a pillow, and remaining suspended on the other cross of the nails. She was glad to be able to return there and take up again almost a spiritual refreshment.

Hard on herself and insatiable in abstinences and bodily tortures, she was on the contrary careful to prevent exaggerations in the sisters regarding the practice of penances, especially if this was to the detriment of good nutrition. In her letters to the superiors she recommends that they not allow imprudences in this matter.

V. THE GREAT LOVES OF MOTHER ROSA

The virginal heart, while it succeeds in freeing the affective potential in order to polarize it in the uncreated Love, increases the capacity to love everything that God loves. Such a polarization becomes all the more fruitful and operative the more vital is the union with the supreme Good.

One of the first manifestations of true love, guided by faith, is piety, the true kind, not devotional or sentimental piety, which interposes itself between the soul and God and takes from love that dynamic restlessness of one who lives not for self but for God and for others. Rosa Gattorno knew how to orient, at the crucial moment of her life, the richness of her affectivity so as to be able to develop an authentic piety centered on the fundamental contents of the faith: the Trinity-God, Jesus Christ, the Virgin Mary, some model saints and protectors, the Church, the Institute, her spiritual daughters, the poor.

1. God, the true Love. The supreme Good

She wrote on the first page of her Memoirs, regarding the decision made in 1858 to give herself fully to God:

«By the grace of the Lord I noticed that all earthly affections were dissipating; nothing was any longer tasty to me: only my God was the pasture of all my delights» (M 1.1, p. 1).

In the fervent colloquies, so frequent, with God, she loves to address Him with appellations of deep meaning: the Being of my living, my All, my Good, the supreme Good, love… She also loves to set her own littleness against the «infinite ocean of God's greatness», that ineffable divine essence in comparison with which «whoever comes to taste it, everything that is earthly serves as nausea» (M 1.2, p. 2). She, who has the experiential light of such greatness, cannot understand «how man can live without knowing God, supreme Good» (M 11.2, p. 785).

God alone suffices

She expresses very often her aspiration, common to all souls accustomed to infused contemplation, to isolate herself from everything that is not God and remain with Him alone. She wrote on 17 January 1875:

«A voice said to me thus:

— Live in God alone and seek nothing else. Converse with Him and seek no other relief than in Him. In Him let everything suffice you…

— Yes, my Good, in you alone!» (M 4.3, p. 15).

There are moments — she says — in which «the world, all creatures are secondary objects, as if divided off, worthy of attention only to gather the fruits to offer to my Good Love» (M 4.3, p. 56).

In the book Labors and Consolations, replying to a «pastor» who tried to disturb her about her walking without a guide, she inserts a beautiful outpouring where she expresses all that God represents in her itinerary of faith:

«I beg you to speak only of the greatness of God and of his omnipotence and mercy. These three subjects alone are a great satisfaction to me, both in hearing them spoken of and in pausing to reason on them alone…

Oh! the mind reasons and in such immensity has room to run without ever finding a stumbling block that stops its reasoning. The intellect develops in the greatest knowledge of the soul in its relations with its God, that endless ocean of greatness, of power and mercy.

The more the mind advances into it, the greater it sees the space and ever new arguments unfold, and the majesty of a God is distinguished in larger proportions. And how the soul is always subject to Him, how it groans painfully when, through the darkness in which it sees itself wrapped because of sin, it feels itself distanced from Him!» (TC, p. 313).

What in her was a maturation of faith, strengthened by unitive experience, she inculcated in the daughters of St. Anne as the goal of the necessary affective purification. On 17 October 1898 she addressed to the novices a warm exhortation on the true love of God, and said to them:

«A religious must always think of Jesus, love Him and be wholly his… What a beautiful thing to be wholly detached from relatives, from superiors, from that sick person, from the confessor!…» (Fiocchi, II, p. 281).

Whoever loves God cannot remain indifferent before the offense against so great a Good. We have already seen to what degree Mother Rosa's heart suffered at seeing God offended. «Only one thing frightens and terrifies me: the offense of God», she repeats in her letters to the superiors.

The Trinity-God

Recalling her contemplations of 1864, she describes, not without some imprecisions in theological terminology, the light received on the mystery of the Trinity, great mystery of love, which of three Persons makes one God, of creative and sanctifying love, which communicates itself to men (M 1.2, p. 1f). On the day of the Resurrection in 1866 she had another infused communication, with vision, on the same mystery (M 1.1, p. 39).

Here we must note her peculiar devotion to the first Person, whom she designates with titles of filial tenderness: my dear eternal Father, dear, lovable, most tender Father, Joy of my soul. The eternal Father defends her in temptations, comforts and sustains her in difficulties, gives her victory in struggles (M 1.1, pp. 75, 78). She strongly recommends to the sisters love of the eternal Father and trust in Him (L to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 22-8-1869, 12-2-1872; to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 15-10-1869, 1-12-1869, 11-6-1871). At the end of her letters she often uses the formula, desired by Fr. Tornatore: «The blessing of our eternal Father be with us». She writes to a superior:

«Love this eternal Father and make your daughters love Him who, if they love this God the Father, our one and only Good, will become perfect and will be able to do whatever they wish, for everything will be done well» (L to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti: 22-5-1871).

In another letter she addresses to the Savior a fervent supplication on behalf of the daughters of St. Anne:

«My Jesus, what more is there in this work, which must be close to your heart, than that your Father be glorified? These poor creatures, daughters of St. Anne, Mother of the Immaculate, carry Him continually on their lips and in all their actions invoke Him, hold Him in their hearts because they love Him as Father… In the end, you may well say: They are the true daughters of my eternal Father, because they expect everything from Him and rest in Him alone…» (L to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 1-6-1871).

The Institute adopted, on the initiative of Fr. Tornatore, most devoted to the first Person of the Trinity, the practice of dedicating the month of

Trust in God's providence

Trust in the divine fatherhood, which Jesus asks of his disciples, is not only, in Mother Rosa's life, an effect of faith, but also a fact experienced almost daily, even in the form of true miracles, in what concerns the Institute's course, especially in economic straits. She often observes the immediate effect of prayer in such situations: an unknown person who brings what is needed to pay a debt, unexpected provisions that arrive from afar at the opportune moment, solution of a difficulty when things seem most entangled… (cf. M 1.1, pp. 71f, 103, 145; 3, pp. 61f, 65f; 4.1, pp. 7, 85-87; 4.4, p. 99f; L to the superior of Fitalia: 12-11-1889).

Usually she does not have recourse to intermediate intercessors, but entrusts herself directly to the most holy Trinity, to the eternal Father. She feels reassured by the promise the Lord made her: «You shall have all that you need» (M 1.1, p. 103, 118). «I was weeping: I told my eternal Father to send me his providence: He appeared to me so beautiful that I remained in ecstasy, and He told me very clearly that

In everything and for everything God's will

In the book Labors and Consolations Mother Rosa imagines a lively dialogue with a «pastor» who would like to dissuade her from going forward, since she walks off the road. She answers every insinuation: «I shall do nothing other than the will of God!». Finally the «pastor» says to her, vexed: «Oh! what a head! your very speech is that of an ignorant creature». To which she replies: «You are right, I have no other science than the will of my Lord!» (TC, pp. 365-367).

Here is the hinge of her spirituality, and also the cause of her intimate anguish, having to face for so many years, alone, the uncertainties of her interior life and the decisions concerning her responsibility as foundress: will it be God's will? This torment, as we have already seen, is present in many pages of her spiritual diary. God's will, God's pleasure, God's good pleasure, God's approval, are synonyms that are also at the center of her pedagogy with the sisters:

«If you knew what consolation I feel merely in pronouncing this word — God's pleasure — and even more, if the sweet thought of being or of being able to come to his delight awakens vividly in me! I feel entirely beside myself, so that if I had to face the cruelest martyrdom, I would feel nothing…» (L to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 4-2-1871). — «A «Thy will be done», said with resignation in time of battles and afflictions, is worth more than having the gift of raising the dead to life» (L to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 20-10-1871).

In the bitter months of 1872, in which she had to suffer so much because of the affair of the Rules, her letters mirror the serenity of her spirit abandoned to God's will. «Let the whole world say: we are doing God's will!» she writes to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa (11-6-1873).

So too in other moments of trials and sufferings. And when it becomes difficult to discover God's will or one must await uncertain future events, there is the disposition of abandonment into God's hands, without ever losing peace:

«Let us put everything into the most holy hands of God; may He do with us as pleases Him» — «Cheerful, without worries, and trust in the Lord» — «Now I have done all my parts, the rest God will do» — «Let us leave it to the Lord, who works everything for the good of our soul» (L to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 1-7-1872; to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 25-1-1869, 6-8-1870, 9-3-1870).

«Let us leave everything in God's hands…; may the divine will be fully accomplished in us: in it everything is satisfied, being for us the sole object of our living» (L to Fr. Donadio: 22-4-1870).

2. Jesus Christ, the Beloved

From all that has been said so far, one could almost speak of a certain theocentrism in the spirituality of Rosa Gattorno. In reality, however, her piety, which is faith and love, opens with all its impetus to the Incarnate God, her beloved Spouse, her Beloved, as she loves to call Him. In the affectionate meditations of Lent 1864 we have a testimony of the intensity of her love for Jesus, concretely for the suffering Jesus (M 2, pp. 77-187). But on every page of her Memoirs, in every letter of hers, Jesus appears as the object of her love, the center of her life.

«When one has Jesus, one has the whole world». — «To grow in the spirit and in the love of Jesus»: this is the ideal of every daughter of St. Anne (L to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 16-12-1868, 1-10-1869; Circ. 1886). She would have wished them all in love, madly in love, with sweet Jesus. «If you knew how much Jesus loves you — she wrote to a postulant —, surely you would be mad for Him and would do nothing else than press Him to your heart and say to Him: Speak to me, command me!» (L to Caterina Rapallino: 1868). «To live for Jesus», «to see Jesus in everything», are frequent recommendations in her letters.

The dear Crucified Love

Following Christ demands readiness and courage; one must answer the Master's invitation like Peter and the other apostles; He is not content with mediocrity, but wants generous hearts: thus Mother Rosa spurs on her daughters (L to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino: 12-2-1867; to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 23-4-1867). Jesus is the model, the mirror in which a daughter of St. Anne must look at herself, learning from Him to find true joy in adversities, to practice the evangelical virtues. One must «make good use of the lessons of such a master and be studious in order to please Him and fully satisfy his will» (L to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 4-2-1871).

She invites them to go to the school of Bethlehem, where the «God made small» offers us splendid lessons of detachment, of annihilation, of poverty. So too she recommends attending the school of Nazareth, which speaks of hiddenness and obedience.

But no chair is richer in profound lessons than that of the school of Calvary.

It was at the beginning of her new life that Rosa Gattorno received from God a sign that was to imprint on her spirituality its most peculiar mark. In her father's house there was a large crucifix before which she spent long hours of the night in prayer. One evening she saw it detach itself from the cross and fall into her arms; she then put it back on the cross, nailing it. The event was repeated a second and a third time. She understood then that she had to accept to live crucified with the crucified Savior 38.

The Crucified will henceforth be her lot, the center of her love, her consoler, guide and master of her existence. In the expression my Crucified, repeated a thousand times, the whole ardor of her heart is felt to vibrate. The favorite theme of her contemplations is that of the Passion of the Lord; more than a meditation, it is a participation in his sufferings, with a longing to arrive at full configuration with Him. She likes to meditate with her head resting at the feet of her Crucified. She closes each of her letters with these or similar words of farewell: «I press you to my Crucified», «Always yours in my dear Crucified», «A strong embrace in my sweet Crucified».

In hard moments of uncertainty or adversity, pressing the cross to her breast, she entrusts herself to Him with assurance: «Oh! my Crucified will take care of everything». «My Crucified will guard his Work». «My Crucified will not abandon his slave». Nothing is more beautiful than the introductory pages of her book Labors and Consolations, where every paragraph begins with the exclamation: My Crucified!

To follow Jesus on the road to Calvary, carrying the cross, and to remain with Him crucified: this is the ideal of her life. She wrote in 1862:

«Now I find myself in the stormy sea, I a poor torn little boat, submerged by the waves: only tightly do I hold to the anchor of the holy Cross, so as not to sink, and to reach the blessed harbor of my Good. Oh! terrible pains!… Press upon my breast the dear standard of the Cross, but join to it the strength to bear it well and climb the mount of sorrow, Calvary and, ever victorious, close to you, to die with you crucified» (M 1.1, p. 23).

In her mystical experiences the sweet embraces of the Crucified are not lacking, such as the one granted her on 18 September 1885 at the moment of Communion: Jesus crucified appeared to her, who detached himself from the cross and embraced her lovingly (M 5.5, p. 1). As foundress she wanted identification with the Crucified to be the yearning of all the daughters of St. Anne. She wrote to one of them:

«Daughter, where are your so cruel pains?… I do not find even so much

38 Testimony of Sr. A. Celsa Speranza, Summ., p. 259, FIOCCHI, II, 210-214. as to relieve the slightest pain of Jesus. Let us try always to reason with the Crucified before us, not at our side 39; let us look in all our actions whether they conform to his exemplar and, then, everything is annihilated, and our sufferings become a fine nothing, less than nothing… (L to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 15-1-1870, 28-2-1870).

The crucified Redeemer is the mediator before the Father. Mother Rosa has unlimited trust in the power of intercession of the blood of the Mediator of the new Covenant, whose voice is more eloquent than that of Abel (Heb 12:24): «Only the blood of my dear Crucified can do all with the heart of his eternal Father: knock and do not tire, for it will be opened to you» (L to Emilia di Fitalia: 5-3-1885).

Her Christocentric piety is not confined to the cross and the sufferings of the Savior. Accustomed to living the paschal mystery in its integrity, she rejoices intensely contemplating the triumph of the Risen One every year, after having participated mystically in the whole Passion on Good Friday.

On Holy Saturday 1862 she lived the jubilation of Jesus' resurrection to such a degree that she could not contain herself for joy and, to restrain its force, began to sing (M 1.1, p. 21). On Easter Sunday 1866 she had a vision of the feast that was being held in heaven, after which she gave vent to her jubilation with an ardent prayer to the risen Lord, to the eternal Father, to the Holy Spirit, to the Virgin Mary (M 1.1, p. 375).

The Sacred Heart of Jesus, school of love

In the course of the 19th century devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus had greatly developed, a development that reached its peak under the pontificate of Leo XII. Rosa Gattorno was not slow to find in the open side of her Beloved the treasure of love. But for her it was always a matter of the Heart of the sweet Crucified. On 2 May 1867, on a night of vigil in the hospital of Cento, she wrote for Caterina Rapallino (later Sr. A. Vincenza) a reflection in the form of a colloquy between Jesus and the bride in which she exhorted her to enter the Heart of Jesus: the
